methodology_note: Source-derived PYQ counts extracted from the user-supplied Physics PDF, with E-M-T-O preserved for 2019–2025. Active topic rows exclude any subtopic with O=0 in both 2024 and 2025, exactly as requested. Chapter-level yearly totals and every source trend/suggestion text are preserved. Excluded-topic labels are listed separately without their historical count rows.
denominator_limit: The PDFs provide annual aggregate counts, not the number of shifts or a complete shift-by-shift question inventory. These values are not probabilities or expected counts for one future shift.
syllabus_limit: Historical/source-authored syllabus comments and study advice are preserved verbatim after whitespace normalization; they are attributed to the source document and are not presented as an independent syllabus verification.
exclusion_rule: A topic is excluded from the active topic matrix only if its source O/Overall count is exactly 0 in both 2024 and 2025. It is listed under excluded_topics by name and PDF page, with no counts. Chapter-level totals remain the source-reported totals; for years before 2024, the chapter total can include excluded topics and therefore may not equal the sum of active topic rows.

chapters.title: Mathematics in Physics
chapters.recent_trend: Error Analysis is a high-scoring and frequently asked topic with increasing weightage over the last 3 years. Vector addition/subtraction is commonly asked, but it saw lower weightage in 2025 than in 2024. Vector Multiplication had no questions in 2025. Lami’s Theorem hasn’t been asked directly in recent years.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Overall, this is an easy chapter. Out of all the topics, error analysis is the most asked and most scoring. So, priority should be given to that during practice. While vector questions are asked less, the basics should be clear because vectors will be used in a lot of the chapters ahead. Just practice PYQs and move on.

chapters.title: Units and Dimensions
chapters.recent_trend: Units rarely have direct questions. Dimensions is a high-weightage topic in 2025, with most questions being easy and quick to master. The difficulty of questions has been consistent over the last 3 years, with slightly better questions in 2025. Frequently asked concepts include dimensional formulae and comparison of dimensions of different quantities. The topic is often tested through Matrix Match questions, with very few numerical problems asked.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Scoring chapter for JEE mains. Units by itself is not a very important topic. Dimensions is very scoring and should be practised thoroughly. It may feel hard to know dimensional formulae of different constants and terms at the start, but as you learn further chapters, you can derive their dimensional formula using formulae you already know, like force, velocity, etc. Only memorise dimensional formulae of the very basic quantities like force, velocity, etc.

chapters.title: Motion In One Dimension

topics.name: Graphs of motion in one dimension

chapters.recent_trend: The weightage of topics has stayed high in 2025 as compared to 2024. Most questions are asked on fundamental topics of rest and motion. A motion under gravity has been asked less recently but had sudden high weightage in 2022. Kinematics is an easy introductory chapter crucial for future mechanics topics, so study it thoroughly. Many students make mistakes with the signs of vector quantities when using formulas. Make sure to practice understanding different graphs; people often get confused here and miss out on easy questions.
chapters.expert_suggestion: It is the Backbone of Mechanics. Most questions are related to fundamental concepts of rest and motion, and also graphical questions. Concepts must be clear regarding graphs and relations between velocity, acceleration, etc. Should pay attention to how we can solve quickly in exams. All concepts will be used in further chapters.

chapters.title: Motion In Two Dimensions
chapters.recent_trend: An important chapter in kinematics. Overall weightage has reduced over the last 3 years Relative motion has the least weightage but fundamentals should be covered. Uniform circular motion had very low weightage in the last two years, but saw high weightage in 2023. Projectile motion has the highest weightage and should be prioritised. Many find it difficult, but practice breaking questions into one-dimensional components. Popular topics also include riverboat and rain-umbrella problems.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Students find it a bit challenging at the start. We need to practice many questions to develop an understanding of breaking down 2D problems into 1D problems. Projectile motion questions are the most frequently asked. Some more advanced questions, like river boat and rain umbrella problems, are very good practice for understanding 2D. Focus on the application of the fundamentals of vectors and their components in this chapter. Uniform circular motion fundamentals should be clear as they are used in further chapters, but are not of very high weightage by themselves.

chapters.title: Laws of Motion
chapters.recent_trend: Overall weightage has decreased in 2025 compared to 2024. Higher weightage is given to the equilibrium of forces and spring forces. The weightage of Newton's laws has reduced in 2025 compared to 2024 Prioritize free body diagrams, as many struggle with basic questions. Typical questions involve pulley systems, masses attached by strings and block-on-block scenarios; some good questions have appeared here. Lack of clarity on frictional force direction is a common cause of errors. Non-uniform circular motion has relatively low weightage. The basics are sufficient. Spring force has low direct question weightage, but its concepts and energy principles must be clear.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Very important chapter for mechanics. High priority should be given to questions for identifying and breakdown down all forces and making force body diagrams, which will be used extensively in further chapters. Common questions where students also find difficulties are pulley systems and block-on- block, which should be practised thoroughly. Conceptual clarity is important for the frictional force, which is the scoring topic. The most important topic is the equilibrium and balancing of forces using Newton’s laws. Practice solving multiple equations in multiple variables for fast solving.

chapters.title: Work Power Energy
chapters.recent_trend: The weightage of topics has stayed similar in 2025 as in 2024. Most questions are asked about energy Direct questions on work done and power are less common than energy, but their fundamentals and concepts must be clear. The weightage of power has slightly decreased, while for circular motion it has increased. Most questions are of moderate difficulty, but with good practice and conceptual clarity, it will become a scoring chapter. 40% of questions are numerical type, so sufficient practice is required for numerical type, too.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Conceptually, not a very difficult chapter. Practice identifying which questions can be solved using the laws of motion and which can be solved faster using the conservation of energy and work-energy theorem. Direct questions related to energy and conservation of energy are more common, but all concepts of work done are important for later chapters. Power is relatively less important, but the basics should be clear. With sufficient practice, this is a scoring chapter overall.

chapters.title: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

topics.name: Centre of mass of discrete particles
Centre of mass of continuous mass distribution

chapters.recent_trend: The weightage of collisions has been reducing since 2024 compared to other years, which had high weightage. There have been no questions on motion of COM and variable mass systems recently, but COM basics should be thoroughly covered. Concepts of momentum should be clear. A good number of questions and an important topic for mechanics. Overall weightage was slightly reduced compared to 2025. Centre of mass of a continuous distribution has low weightage and tough questions; overall, less priority. Impulse questions aren't usually tough, but students struggle with conceptual clarity. 33% of questions are numerical, so practice in this area should be good.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Collision is an important topic, even if its weightage is not that high. Students can memorise some common centres of mass values, like a hemisphere, semicircular disc, etc. But it is more important to remember how they are derived, so you will be able to find the centre of mass for any mass distribution. Momentum and its conservation are frequently used in future chapters. Collisions will be clear if concepts of momentum and energy are thorough.

chapters.title: Rotational Motion

topics.name: Moment of inertia of rigid bodies

chapters.recent_trend: Many tough questions are asked. Students also find this to be one of the hardest chapters. Overall weightage has increased in 2025 compared to 2024. There are significantly fewer questions on the moment of inertia of rigid bodies. Increased weightage from angular momentum and angular impulse in 2025. Very few questions on collisions in rotation can be skipped if needed. Very few questions on combination of translational and rotational motion. Basics are sufficient. Considering previous years, moment of inertia should still be a high-priority topic since it is the basis of all further topics. Rolling motion without slipping is considered one of the toughest for students, but a decent number of questions are asked. 40% of questions are numerical type so the practice of numericals should be good.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Overall, one of the hardest chapters, which students find difficult to understand. You should remember the moment of inertia of some common shapes, like rods, spheres, etc. Torque balancing is similar to force balancing. Students make mistakes in the direction of torque. Angular momentum and its conservation should be conceptually clear. Applying all these concepts together, students can tackle the difficult rolling questions, which should be done step by step by breaking them down into different force-balancing and torque-balancing equations. Overall, more practice is needed for this chapter to become proficient. It's fine if students do not get full conceptual clarity in their first attempt.

chapters.title: Gravitation
chapters.recent_trend: Low weightage in 2025 as compared to 2024. High-weightage topics are acceleration due to gravity and gravitational potential in last 3 years. Newton’s law of gravitation and gravitational field have fewer questions in exams, but a strong conceptual understanding is essential as they form the foundation of the chapter. Kepler’s laws and satellite motion are tougher but important, and should be attempted after mastering the basics. Most formulae of Gravitation are analogous to Electrostatics.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Considered to be a moderate-difficult chapter. High weightage. Newton’s law of gravitation and gravitational fields are asked about sometimes, but often not directly. Gravitational potential and acceleration due to gravity are the most important, and all concepts of these topics should be clear. One bonus of this chapter is that if students have clarity in this chapter, they find electrostatics to be easier later on. Focus on identifying concepts used in questions. With enough practice of gravitational potential, students can tackle satellite problems.

chapters.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids

topics.name: Work Done in Stretching a Wire

chapters.recent_trend: This chapter has shown consistent weightage in recent years, with most questions focused on Young’s Modulus and breaking stress. Other topics are rarely asked, but a clear understanding of Elasticity basics is essential as they form the foundation of the chapter. Bulk modulus basics are sufficient. Work done in stretching wire and shearing stress can be skipped. 40% of questions are numerical, so practice of numerical should be good.
chapters.expert_suggestion: This chapter tends to be neglected by some students, but it is scoring with basic practice. It has very consistent weightage, and almost all weightage comes from Young's Modulus and breaking stress. So this takes the highest priority. Some topics, like work done by stretching a wire and shearing stress, can be skipped if needed. Usually, this chapter follows a consistent question pattern and takes less time to master.

chapters.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids
chapters.recent_trend: Weightage has remained constant in the last 3 years compared to other years. Highest weighted topics are surface tension and viscosity. Surface tension can be a confusing topic and tough questions can be asked from it, so a lot of practice is required. No direct questions on the density of fluids; the concept is sufficient. Efflux of liquid and Pascal’s law have minimal weightage—basic understanding is sufficient. Archimedes principle questions tend to be on the harder side, but weightage is negligible. Around 30% of the questions are numerical, so strong numerical practice is recommended.
chapters.expert_suggestion: The weightage of this chapter has increased in 2024 & 2025. Students find this to be a slightly confusing chapter. Fundamentals like density, Pascal's law, efflux of fluid, etc, should be conceptually clear and their basics should be practised. Surface tension and viscosity are high-weightage topics that students find more challenging. Importance should be given to the theoretical understanding of these topics, as tough questions can be made from these. Overall, it may take more than 1 attempt to have a satisfactory conceptual understanding in this chapter. Reynolds' number has been removed from the syllabus, so other topics of viscosity are more important now.

chapters.title: Oscillations
chapters.recent_trend: The chapter's weightage remained constant in both 2024 and 2025. Most questions are based on standard equations of time, focusing on period, angular frequency, and occasionally energy. In 2023, direct questions on Energy of SHM were seen, but they were nearly absent in 2024 and 2025. Students often spend excessive time on Applications of SHM, despite its low weightage. About 40% of the questions are numerical, so strong numerical practice is important.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Students find it challenging at the start. We need to practice many questions to develop an understanding. Fundamental questions are being asked on the equation of SHM, time period, frequency, and energy calculations. Applications of SHM can be tricky for students, and they will need multiple rounds of revision to master.
chapters.source_notes: Qs in this chapter marked with ^ denotes out of syllabus but good to solve qs

chapters.title: Waves and Sound
chapters.recent_trend: The weightage of this chapter remained constant in both 2024 and 2025. Organ Pipe (Vibration of Air Column) emerged as the most favored topic in 2025. Doppler’s Effect has been completely removed from the syllabus, so no need to spend time on its lengthy problems. The basics of Mechanical Waves have been the most scoring area in 2025 and 2024. Around 40% of the questions are numerical, so regular practice is essential. Students often over-visualize concepts and get confused—focusing on formulae is usually sufficient.
chapters.expert_suggestion: The most challenging topic Doppler Effect, has been removed from the syllabus of JEE Mains. No need to go in-depth, you should just know all the formulae, especially for organ pipe (open and closed), speed of wave in medium & equation of transverse and longitudinal waves. Similar types of questions are repeatedly asked in PYQs.
chapters.source_notes: Qs in this chapter marked with * denotes out of syllabus qs

chapters.title: Thermal Properties of Matter
chapters.recent_trend: The weightage of this chapter has increased in 2025 compared to 2024. Calorimetry and radiation are likely to carry higher weightage. Calorimetry is a scoring topic and relatively easy to grasp. Newton’s law of cooling has been removed from the JEE Main syllabus. Only a single question has been asked onThermal expansion in 2025. Thermometry has had a few questions in 2025, though it was previously not commonly asked. About 30% of the questions are numerical, so solid numerical practice is important.
chapters.expert_suggestion: This chapter has fluctuating weightage but is not very difficult to cover. We used to see a high weightage of this chapter, but it had an exceptionally low weightage in 2024, and other chapters of Thermal Physics are more important comparatively. Calorimetry is of high weightage and is most scoring. In the transmission of heat, radiation has the highest priority, fundamentals of conduction are sufficient, and it is fine if you just know the concept of convection. Thermometry basics are important, as questions have started to be asked recently.
chapters.source_notes: Qs in this chapter marked with * denotes out of syllabus qs and ^ denotes out of syllabus but good to solve qs

chapters.title: Thermodynamics

topics.name: Heat Engine, Refrigerator and Second Law of Thermodynamics

chapters.recent_trend: The chapter has seen a significant increase in weightage in 2025, despite a reduction in the syllabus. The Carnot engine is completely removed which used to have decent weightage before 2024. Most important topic is Thermodynamic Processes and we need to practice this well from PYQs. A solid understanding of the First Law of Thermodynamics is crucial before attempting Thermodynamic Processes. Over the past 6 years, more than 40 special-type questions have been asked, with a strong emphasis on graph-based problems.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Questions from the first law of thermodynamics are easy, you just need to take care of the sign convention of U, Q, and W. Most questions are from the thermodynamics process. There are Graphs and equations in different processes. The Carnot engine is removed from the syllabus, which used to have very high weightage earlier.
chapters.source_notes: Qs in this chapter marked with * denotes out of syllabus qs and ^ denotes out of syllabus but good to solve qs

chapters.title: Kinetic Theory of Gases

topics.name: Degree of Freedom and Specific Heat

chapters.recent_trend: The chapter's weightage increased in 2024 but dropped significantly in 2025. Earlier, speed of gas dominated with most of the questions focused on it. In 2025, several moderate-level questions have been asked on Degree of Freedom and Specific Heat. Practicing direct questions on Pressure and Energy of gas can help score well. In the last 3 years, theoretical questions—especially Multi-statement and Assertion-Reason types —have been common.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Overall, the Low Input High Output chapter. We get so many questions on the degree of freedom, heat capacity, pressure, and speed of gas. Just don’t get confused between degrees of freedom for different molecules (linear, diatomic, non-linear), you will get a lot of questions involving degrees of freedom. Speed of gas was the trending topic, which drastically reduced in weightage in the last 2 years. Expect the unexpected.

chapters.title: Electrostatics

topics.name: Electric Field and Electric Field Lines

chapters.recent_trend: The chapter's weightage in 2025 is very similar to that of 2024. Electric field, Electric field lines, and coulomb law are repetitively asked concepts in the last 3 years. Electric Potential and Potential Energy weightage is reduced in 2024 but the questions are more tricky in last 3 years. Formula-based questions of Electric Flux and Gauss' Law are essential even if you don't want to spend time on tough questions. Should practice understanding different types of dipole arrangement and make a formula list for revision.
chapters.expert_suggestion: This chapter is a prerequisite for the entire Electromagnetism. And in recent years, it has increased in difficulty. A few difficult problems have been asked. But you cannot neglect this chapter. Do not get bogged down by the amount of concepts and formulae. The majority of formulae of field and potential are analogous to gravitation. Do not miss Electric Flux and Gauss Law, even if it takes some extra time.

chapters.title: Capacitance

topics.name: Force and Energy stored in capacitor

chapters.recent_trend: The chapter's weightage has remained consistent over the last three years. Charging and discharging of capacitors has seen a steady rise in importance. Capacitors with dielectrics require practice to become familiar with the common question patterns. 35% of questions are numerical type so practice of numerical should be good. There’s no need to go too deep into complex RC circuits, as their weightage is low.
chapters.expert_suggestion: It is a tricky chapter, taking care of units and values. Generally, dielectric questions are asked to find energy, charge, and force on a dielectric; a combination of capacitors is very important. Just learn the formulas and practice a good number of questions to get hold of this chapter. Don't get scared by charging and discharging; we only get formula-based questions.

chapters.title: Current Electricity

topics.name: Electric Current and Drift of Electrons
Electric Power and Heating Effect of Current

chapters.recent_trend: Color coding of resistors and Potentiometer is removed from the JEE Main syllabus. The chapter’s weightage decreased in 2025 compared to 2024. Combination of resistances questions have significantly reduced in 2025 and 2024. In 2025, direct questions about the Electric Power and Heating Effect of Current are asked. Questions on Resistance and Resistivity continue to appear frequently. Very few questions were asked about electric instruments in 2025 compared to 2024. Around 35% of the questions are numerical, so solid numerical practice is important.
chapters.expert_suggestion: The Most Important chapter for JEE physics. You need to practice multiple different circuit-based questions, but once you get habitual, you will be able to solve questions very fast. Focus on electrical instruments, even if the Potentiometer is removed from the syllabus. Practice PYQs on how to find equivalent resistance in different situations.

chapters.title: Magnetic Properties of Matter
chapters.recent_trend: Earths magnetic field is removed from Jee main syllabus and weightage of this chapter is almost nil now. We got some questions on Magnetism and Properties of Magnet, especially the Bar magnet, in recent years. Magnetic Equipments is completely removed from the syllabus. No need to overspend time on this chapter, cover PYQs and move on. Come back for revision before exam.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Earth's magnetism is completely removed from the syllabus, and no tricky questions have been asked recently. Focus only on NCERT-specific concepts, as most of the questions have a repeated pattern. Quickly cover the PYQs of the must-do bucket and move on to the next chapter.

chapters.title: Magnetic Effects of Current

topics.name: Biot-Savart’s Law and Ampere’s Circuital Law
Motion of Charged Particle in Magnetic Field
Force and Torque on Current Carrying Conductor

chapters.recent_trend: The chapter’s weightage dropped in 2025 compared to 2024. Since 2020, very few theoretical questions have been asked. Earlier, Magnetic Field dominated the weightage, but now questions are spread across all topics. Motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field includes a mix of easy and moderate-level questions in 2025 Force and torque on a current-carrying conductor tend to be more on the difficult side. For JEE Main, formula-based questions on Magnetic Moment are generally sufficient.
chapters.expert_suggestion: It is a High Input High Output chapter, you need to learn thoroughly all the concepts, mostly questions are asked about moving particles and magnetic field, force, and torque experienced by the conductor in a magnetic field. The good part is that once we remember useful formulae, we can solve questions very quickly. You can leave very tricky questions for JEE Advanced.

chapters.title: Electromagnetic Induction

topics.name: Magnetic Flux, Faraday's and Lenz law

chapters.recent_trend: There has been a noticeable reduction in the weightage of EMI in the JEE Main syllabus. The weightage of Motional and Rotational EMF dropped significantly in 2024 and 2025, which was unexpected. Self and Mutual Inductance appeared less frequently in 2025 compared to 2024, but the questions were straightforward. Around 45% of the questions are numerical, so strong numerical practice is important. Special-type questions are rarely asked in this chapter.
chapters.expert_suggestion: It is a tough chapter, practice a good amount of questions from rotational and motional emf, Inductance with 50% numerical questions where guesswork will not be useful. Limit to must-do questions only if you struggling in this chapter and revision is mandatory to get hold of this chapter.

chapters.title: Alternating Current
chapters.recent_trend: Overall, the chapter's weightage has decreased in 2025 compared to previous years. The weightage of AC Circuits has reduced since 2023 and 2022 Many students struggle with basic concepts of Alternating Current, Voltage, and Power, so these should be prioritised during preparation. While Quality Factor has been removed from the syllabus, Power Factor should not be overlooked. Focus on various circuit types—LR, LCR, RC, etc.—and practice drawing phase diagrams. Transformers may seem moderate initially but become easy after one thorough revision. About 35% of the questions are numerical, so consistent practice is essential. Matrix Match, Graphical and Statement-based questions have been frequently asked in lat 3 years
chapters.expert_suggestion: It is a scoring chapter, formula questions are asked from basic LCR circuits, current, voltage drop, and resonance conditions. Don't get too much into parallel circuits, they are irrelevant for JEE mains. Quality factor is removed from the syllabus but we still get questions on Power Factor.
chapters.source_notes: Qs in this chapter marked with * denotes out of syllabus qs

chapters.title: Ray Optics

topics.name: Reflection of Light from Plane Mirror
Mirror Formula, Reflection in Spherical Mirror
Critical angle and total internal reflection
Refraction of light from plane surface
Lens Formula, Refraction of light from curved surface

chapters.recent_trend: The chapter saw a drastic increase in weightage in 2025 compared to 2024 & questions became tougher in 2025. Lens Formula and Refraction from curved surfaces have consistently held their weightage in 2025. In 2025, questions were asked from combination of Lenses and Mirrors, as well as the Human Eye. Traditional moderate-level questions from Prism and Dispersion of Light were also seen. Graph-based questions can be tricky, so practicing all relevant PYQs is important. While Resolving Power has been removed from the syllabus, questions on the Microscope and Telescope can still appear. Around 35% of the questions are numerical, so solid numerical practice is essential.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Tricky and Lengthy chapter where only formulas will not work. The sign convention should be clear to you before starting the questions. Most questions are asked about refraction through plane and curved surfaces, a combination of lenses, and formula-based questions on optical instruments. We started getting tricky questions of multiple lenses or mixed questions of lenses and mirrors that are inclined towards JEE Advanced.
chapters.source_notes: Qs in this chapter marked with * denotes out of syllabus qs

chapters.title: Wave Optics
chapters.recent_trend: Overall weightage has stayed same in 2025 like 2024. Youngs Double Slit Experiment is the highlight of the last three years. No need to spend time on Special Cases in YDSE. Diffraction of Light weightage was increased in 2024. Refer to NCERT for theory. Direct questions of Polarization of Light are not so common in 2025. 40% of questions are numerical type so practice of numerical should be good.
chapters.expert_suggestion: This is an important and scoring chapter. Questions mostly from YDSE and polarisation are asked. For YDSE, go through all cases of it(including the general case). For polarisation, go through the NCERT and do PYQs. Diffraction and wavefront questions are also asked sometimes, which can be confusing. If you have less time, then skip this part.

chapters.title: Dual Nature of Matter
chapters.recent_trend: The chapter's weightage remained consistent in 2025, similar to 2024. In 2025, the Photoelectric Effect dominated the questions from this chapter. Matter Waves questions are generally easy but were more frequent before 2024. Graph-based questions have been easy and commonly asked in the last three years. Numerical-type questions are rare from this chapter.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Easy Kill chapter for both mains and advanced. Read NCERT and practice PYQs for mains. For advanced theory is the same, but practice questions of the advanced bucket. Questions are mostly asked about the photoelectric effect. Do memorise the formula and also the graphs. Graphs can be confusing at times.
chapters.source_notes: Qs in this chapter marked with * denotes out of syllabus qs

chapters.title: Atomic Physics
chapters.recent_trend: The chapter’s weightage decreased in 2025 compared to 2024 and 2023. In 2025 Bohr's Atomic Model was the highlight with slightly less weightage of Atomic Spectrum. In 2025 Atomic Spectrum was the highlight with slightly less weightage of Bohr's Atomic Model. We get very few questions from Atomic Models in recent years. 36% of questions are numerical type so practice of numerical should be good.
chapters.expert_suggestion: An easy and scoring chapter if you cover the Structure of Atom in Chemistry. Direct formula based chapter with questions mostly from Bohr's model and atomic spectrum. Doing NCERT and PYQs are enough. Atomic structure and models have no importance, so skip them.

chapters.title: Nuclear Physics
chapters.recent_trend: Overall weightage was decreased in 2025 as comapred to 2024. Even though Radioactivity was removed from the syllabus, 2 questions were still asked in 2025. Nuclear Energy and Nuclear Reactions now feature more lengthy and detailed questions. Loliop questions are asked from the Nuclear structure. Numericals of this chapter are lengthy, there is no need to get surprised in the exam.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Weightage is consistent even after Radioactivity is deleted from the syllabus. Nuclear structure and nuclear energy are important topics, so keep their theory and formulas in hand. Don't get bogged down by lengthy calculations. Focus on practice so you don't get a shock in tests.
chapters.source_notes: Qs in this chapter marked with * denotes out of syllabus qs

chapters.title: Electromagnetic Waves
chapters.recent_trend: The chapter’s weightage has seen a bit dip in 2025 as compared to 2024. Most questions are based on equations of EM waves and Maxwell’s equations. NCERT is the key resource—revise its tables and concepts thoroughly. Matrix Match questions have been the most frequent in recent years. Numerical-type questions are less commonly asked in this chapter.
chapters.expert_suggestion: Low Input High Output chapter, don't leave it for the last days. Formula-based questions from equations of EM waves and Maxwell equations are very common and repeated multiple times in PYQs. Revise the EM spectrum and examples given in the NCERT, and we get direct questions from the NCERT table.

chapters.title: Semiconductors
chapters.recent_trend: Junction Transistors are removed from the JEE Mains syllabus. Weightage remained similar in 2025, just like in 2024. Logic Gates are a must-do, even if you plan to skip other parts of the chapter. Several moderate-level questions on Diodes are asked, often requiring a good understanding of Current Electricity. No need to spend time on Rectifier as no question is asked in last 3 years.
chapters.expert_suggestion: It is a scoring chapter, but some students find it difficult at the start. If you are among them, then just do the logic gates part. If you are comfortable, then go with diodes too. Do these from the NCERT only, and then move to PYQs. You can get a grasp on this chapter only by doing this much.

chapters.title: Communication System
chapters.recent_trend: Completely removed from the JEE Mains syllabus. Most students just remember direct formulae of modulation to score in state exams. Weightage used to be very high before 2024. Modulation was my favorite topic. Propagation of EM Waves is not useful for even state exams.
chapters.expert_suggestion: This chapter is removed from JEE Mains, and most students never study this chapter. Solve PYQs only if you are preparing for other state exams and BITSAT.

chapters.title: Experimental Physics
chapters.recent_trend: The chapter’s weightage decreased in 2025 compared to 2024. Vernier Caliper and Screw Gauge remain the two most important topics. Ensure you're comfortable with the various terminologies used in instruments. There’s no need to study the entire Lab Manual, as it's not directly relevant for the exam.
chapters.expert_suggestion: It is a very easy chapter. Just a few experiments from overall physics, which are very simple and can be covered at one go if you are thorough with physics. Memorise formulae for screw gauge and verier calipers and go through problem-solving to learn how to solve problems. No need to overspend time on the lab manual for this chapter.
